items.title: Behind India’s IIT dream: Student suicides and gaps in support
items.summary: Rishikesh Kumar made it to IIT, but died months later in a suspected suicide, reviving questions about student support.

items.summary: Heavy rains affect 2,000 families in Peru's Piura and 47,000 people in Ecuador, where 34 deaths have been reported.

items.summary: Albanese's detention poses a test for Costa Rica's candidate, Rebeca Grynspan, who has led the UN's recent straw poll.

items.summary: Analysts say that shifting tactics, names and geography challenge claims of win against Kashmir's separatist movement.

items.summary: MSF says premises 'clearly marked' with its logos, location communicated to and known by Israeli military.

items.title: Parts of US clean up after Thanksgiving storm lashes East Coast
items.summary: Power is being slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers following a round of heavy wind, rain and snow.

items.title: Bulgarians demand action by French after Marseille match violence
items.summary: Bulgarians protested at the French embassy after violence at a Europa League match hospitalised six Levski Sofia fans.

items.title: Hunted beyond borders: Allegations of Tanzanian repression in Kenya
items.summary: The case of a missing activist raises fears for the safety of Tanzanian dissidents.

items.title: Taiwan votes in local elections to choose mayors, other leaders
items.summary: Key mayoral race in Taipei, a stronghold of the opposition Kuomintang, tests the governing Democratic Progressive Party.

items.summary: An Israeli strike on a clinic operated by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in Gaza has killed two watchmen.

items.summary: Anger and frustration erupt over record-high electricity rates, surging cost of living and deteriorating basic services.

items.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese accuses Costa Rican authorities of defamation after being denied entry.

items.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says the drone behind the deadly Kuwait strike was made in Iran.

items.title: At least eight found dead on migrant boat off Spain’s Canary Islands
items.summary: Six people airlifted to hospital in serious condition, Spanish rescue service says.

items.summary: The US military says it disabled a commercial ship after it left an Iranian port and ignored warnings to stop.

items.title: Will Taiwan vote to revive nuclear power – and why does that matter for AI?
items.summary: Voters will decide on Saturday whether to scrap the country's 'nuclear-free homeland' policy.

items.title: Kenyan cult leader guilty of manslaughter more than 123 starvation deaths
items.summary: Paul Mackenzie, already serving 200 years, is the founder and pastor of the Good News International Church.

items.title: US military says it disabled merchant ship trying to breach Iran blockade
items.summary: The US military says it disabled the Palau-flagged ship’s propulsion but its crew was unharmed.

items.title: ‘Activists of rhythm’: Fighting Spain’s far-right through art
items.summary: Madrid’s La Parceria and Espacio Afro cultural centres are using the arts to fight racism and boost migrant voices.

items.title: Why are families going hungry in northern Yemen even where food is on sale?
items.summary: Flour and oil still reach markets in Hodeidah and Sanaa. But high costs and lack of work and aid put it out of reach.

items.title: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks
items.summary: The number of Indians working in Germany has grown rapidly in recent years. But many continue to face challenges in the labor market. Some also fall victim to recruitment scams, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.

items.title: Polls open in Taiwan's closely watched local elections
items.summary: Polls have opened for local elections in Taiwan. While campaigners have stayed away from the topic of China and focused on issues like transport and childcare, Beijing has repeatedly weighed in.

items.title: Spain's Sanchez makes final appeal to voters before election
items.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez told people to turn out in large numbers so the country does not go "backwards." Polls suggest an end to his eight-year leftist leadership of Spain.

items.title: US disables ship in Gulf of Oman under Iran blockade
items.summary: The United States said it was continuing "to strictly enforce the blockade" of Iran's ports. Meanwhile, Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador over a strike that killed two Italian technicians.

items.title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
items.summary: Quebec's government passed Bill 21 to ban religious symbols for public servants, arguing it was necessary to protect its secularist society. Critics argue the bill weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.

items.title: Germany news: Lawmakers approve debt-laden 2027 budget
items.summary: German lawmakers voted on a federal budget which foresees €556 billion in spending. Elsewhere, the Left Party is hosting a summit on femicide and the BSW party conference starts in Dresden. DW has more.

items.title: Spanish rider Marc Marquez announces MotoGP retirement, days after clinching record 8th world title
items.summary: Marc Marquez took fans and his team by surprise when announcing this weekend's race in Valencia will be his last. The 33-year-old won a record eight MotoGP titles, including his rookie and retirement seasons.

items.title: France seeks German man in Channel migrant boat probe
items.summary: A German businessman is accused of supplying equipment to smugglers organizing migrant crossings from France to the United Kingdom. However, he can't face formal charges until he is extradited to France.

items.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit
items.summary: An EU leaders summit on the bloc's seven-year budget fell apart amid divisions over how to fund Ukraine. The budget proposal also includes a 3% tax on US tech companies, in a bid for the EU to generate additional funds.

items.title: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, Brussels' most anticipated new art museum, opens its doors
items.summary: A major addition to Europe's cultural scene: Kanal-Centre Pompidou, the new contemporary art museum in a former Citroen factory complex, is celebrating its opening with a free, nonstop weekend program.

items.title: Serbia's Student List runs chemistry professor Radomir Saicic for president
items.summary: After ousting strongman Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's student movement has now nominated academic Radomir Saicic for the upcoming presidential vote. Saicic accused the "outgoing regime" of trying to collapse the state.

items.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
items.summary: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.

items.title: Arsenic in the water: Thailand presses Myanmar over mining pollution
items.summary: Thailand is seeking to tackle river pollution stemming from rare earth mines in neighboring Myanmar. The two countries held joint talks this week as a "first step towards agreeing on the evidence."

items.title: Georgia: Police clash with Besiktas fans at Israel club game
items.summary: Turkey's Besiktas accused Georgian police of using "disproportionate" force during the game with Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva, which saw Besiktas fans unfurl a banner supporting Palestine.

items.title: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
items.summary: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.

items.title: As Gambia gears up for election, can Barrow secure a third term?
items.summary: President Adama Barrow is seeking a third term as Gambians vote on December 5. The election will test the opposition's appeal and the country's progress on democratic reform.

items.title: Informer TV owner Vucicevic arrested: Has the reckoning with Serbia's pro-Vucic media machine begun?
items.summary: The arrest of media owner Dragan J. Vucicevic raises questions about whether Serbia is holding the people behind the country's pro-Vucic media accountable — or whether this is another political power struggle.

items.title: Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?
items.summary: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte faces trial in The Hague over his deadly war on drugs. The proceedings could determine the political fortunes of a powerful dynasty. Victims' families hope to see justice.

items.title: In Iran, child marriage risks complicated by war
items.summary: War, poverty and disrupted schooling could put more girls in Iran at risk of child marriage, rights advocates have warned.

items.title: Philippines: VP Duterte says father's ICC case 'not a fair trial'
items.summary: Sara Duterte has said the ICC will not give her father a fair trial and that the Hague-based court wants to "make a statement." Duterte alleges the case against her father is politically motivated.

items.title: The tiny BSW is a party in crisis, as it is set to hand the far-right AfD power in eastern Germany
items.summary: Sahra Wagenknecht's BSW party is set to disrupt German politics yet again. Espousing a mix of left-wing economic policy and populist far-right anti-migration rhetoric, it now stands to play kingmaker to the far right AfD

items.title: Russia sports ban: Ukraine's Heraskevych hails EU pushback
items.summary: As European countries challenge Russia's sporting return, Ukrainian Olympian Vladyslav Heraskevych believes the IOC is facing a "very big crisis."

items.title: How East Germany boosted Vietnam's coffee industry
items.summary: When East Germany could no longer afford to import coffee, it introduced a substitute blend containing rye and chicory in 1977. A public outcry ensued. The solution to the problem lay 9,000 kilometers away — in Vietnam.

items.title: AI goes from math dunce to genius
items.summary: It once struggled to get simple sums right. But AI is now tackling tough mathematical problems like the Riemann hypothesis. How AI made this extraordinary leap — and why mathematicians should be "deeply worried."

items.title: German Catholic Church abuse victims may receive higher compensation
items.summary: In a landmark ruling, judges in Cologne found the Catholic Church responsible for abuse committed by clergy members. Victims could now be entitled to more compensation.

items.title: Albania's youth are protesting, no longer leaving the country
items.summary: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.

items.title: Trial of Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia begins after delay
items.summary: Despite delays due to health issues, the trial of the Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia has begun. Prosecutors say the defendant used her military contacts to provide information on German defense and Ukraine.

items.title: On farewell trip, Steinmeier calls for more investment in Africa
items.summary: Cote d'Ivoire, Ghana, Kenya: On his last trip to Africa, outgoing German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier called on companies at home to be bolder and seize opportunities in Africa.

items.title: Freigang banned — Germany star to miss 2027 World Cup
items.summary: Germany forward Laura Freigang has been suspended until October 2027 after missing three doping tests, ruling her out of next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil. Freigang has denied any intention to evade controls.

items.title: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
items.summary: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.

items.title: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain
items.summary: The agreement offers new export and investment opportunities for Jakarta and Brussels. But can Indonesia turn Europe's growing interest in its markets and critical minerals into sustainable gains at home?

items.title: Joshua Kimmich critcizes Bayern bosses over Musiala health comments
items.summary: Joshua Kimmich has slammed Bayern Munich's leadership over comments about Jamal Musiala's health issues. The bosses have questioned whether the player can return to previous form – and is still worth his high salary.

items.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast
items.summary: Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker capsized off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.

items.title: Germany news: Cologne court awards record damages in Catholic sex abuse case
items.summary: A court has awarded the highest damages ever in Germany to a victim of sexual abuse linked to the Catholic Church. An alleged spy and suspected terrorists are also making headlines in Germany on Thursday.

items.title: Germany: 2 arrested, suspected of plotting synagogue attack
items.summary: Federal prosecutors say they have ordered the arrest of two members of a pro-Iranian group on suspicion of planning an attack on a synagogue. They were detained in the cities of Heidelberg and Cologne.

items.title: Russia-Ukraine war extends to Baltic, Mediterranean
items.summary: By attacking Russian vessels around the world, Ukraine is trying to increase the pressure on Russia and also sending out signals to its Western allies. What is the impact on global maritime trade?

items.title: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
items.summary: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine?

items.title: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
items.summary: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.

items.title: €561 Billion and Still Not Enough: Germany's 2027 Budget Exposes a Coalition on the Brink
items.summary: The budget for 2027 has reached new highs, and pension funds, defense spending and a weak economy are increasing the pressure. At the same time, tensions are mounting within the government.

items.title: German firms eye Africa as global trade shocks hit traditional markets
items.summary: German businesses are optimistic about Africa, but Berlin's cautious approach to risk is holding them back from cashing in on the opportunities that their competitors from countries like the UAE and Turkey are seizing.

items.title: Ice hockey prospect Max Calce follows Leon Draisaitl's path, leaving Mannheim for Canada
items.summary: The player widely seen as Germany's biggest ice hockey talent to come along in years is leaving the country's top professional league for Canada – changing tracks in his bid to make it to the NHL.

items.title: Climate loss and damage fund exists, but the money doesn't
items.summary: Climate-vulnerable countries fought for years to create a loss and damage fund. Four years on, demand far outstrips funding, pledges are scarce, and disaster-hit nations are still waiting for support.

items.title: Germany's women's football team take stand against domestic violence
items.summary: Germany's women's football team are to wear UN Women badges in games against Argentina and Peru, as domestic violence hits a record high in Germany.

items.title: German auto workers on back foot as costs, competition bite
items.summary: German auto workers profited during the industry's boom years, but are now increasingly being asked to trade past gains for future job security.

items.title: Domestic violence soars to record high in Germany
items.summary: Every three days in Germany, a man kills his wife or ex-partner. Every 10 minutes, the police record a sexual offense against a woman. "A shocking finding," according to Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig.

items.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

items.title: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
items.summary: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.

items.title: CAS reinstates Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions
items.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions, overturning a CAF decision that stripped them of the title. Morocco, previously declared winners, are confirmed runners-up.

items.title: Bombed factories, billion-dollar opportunity: Why German companies are staying in Ukraine
items.summary: German companies remain committed to Ukraine despite million-dollar losses, an unreliable energy supply and a shortage of skilled workers. They are betting on new markets and long-term growth.

items.title: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble
items.summary: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.

items.title: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award
items.summary: Two German film students confronted the American who won festival prizes with their animated movie. "The Talented Mr. F," their documentary on their fight against plagiarism, is now in the spotlight.

items.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
items.summary: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.

items.title: Weapons, war and wavering trust: Germans want to see more restraint in foreign policy
items.summary: According to a study by the Körber Foundation, a growing number of Germans now oppose providing military aid to Ukraine. The majority also believes that Germany should take a neutral position between the US and China.

items.title: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035
items.summary: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first World Cup since 1966.

items.title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
items.summary: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.

items.title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
items.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset.

items.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
items.summary: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

items.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
items.summary: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

items.title: COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy
items.summary: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?

items.title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
items.summary: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.

items.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
items.summary: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.

items.title: Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism
items.summary: Numerous grassroots initiatives in Germany are facing funding cuts. Affected organizations are sounding the alarm, pointing to growing challenges posed by far-right extremism.

items.title: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect
items.summary: A new project and exhibition, "The Night Watch Lives," lifts the veil on the hidden world of microbes covering one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.

items.title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
items.summary: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.

items.title: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
items.summary: Germany's biggest union is calling for more strikes over heated pay disputes with car makers like Mercedes and shipyards among the companies impacted. Meanwhile, a Berlin hospital fire leaves many injured.

items.title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
items.summary: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study has found, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.

items.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
items.summary: After two weeks of tough talks, the COP31 climate summit has closed without a consensus on how to quit fossil fuels or fund countries struggling to adapt to a hotter world.

items.title: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029
items.summary: "The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the political landscape?

items.title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
items.summary: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.

items.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
items.summary: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

items.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
items.summary: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

items.title: EU takes aim at tech giants in tax proposal
items.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

items.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
items.summary: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

items.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
items.summary: Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.

items.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
items.summary: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

items.title: COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading
items.summary: Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?

items.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
items.summary: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

items.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
items.summary: Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?

items.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
items.summary: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.

items.title: Germany face Belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
items.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.

items.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
items.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

items.title: Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
items.summary: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

items.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?
items.summary: Two challengers to Gianni Infantino have registered for next year's FIFA presidential election. What do Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima stand for – and do they stand a chance against the incumbent?

items.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports
items.summary: According to a letter obtained by the media, Lufthansa's executive board said the German company is losing €20 million every month. In addition to job cuts, operational cuts are also planned.

items.title: Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?
items.summary: From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?

items.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
items.summary: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

items.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
items.summary: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.

items.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
items.summary: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.

items.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
items.summary: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.

items.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
items.summary: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

items.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
items.summary: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

items.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
items.summary: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.

items.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
items.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

items.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
items.summary: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

items.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine
items.summary: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

items.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
items.summary: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?

items.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
items.summary: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

items.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
items.summary: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.

items.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
items.summary: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.

items.title: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
